correctness.rationale: The source paper supplies a contraction H with extremal eigenvalues +1 and -1 for the standard sparse-grid transport operator. Von Neumann's polynomial inequality reduces the nonnormal fully discrete operator norm to an origin-tangent scalar stability disk. For SSPRK(3,3), a symbolic Bernstein-basis factorization proves disk inclusion exactly up to the unique positive root of 2 mu^3 - 3 mu^2 + 3 mu - 3, while the alternating mode gives a matching instability witness above the root. A standalone symbolic and finite-matrix verification agrees with the proof.

originality.rationale: The scalar Runge--Kutta stability-disk problem and SSP theory are prior art and are not claimed as new. Huang's 2026 preprint states only the SSP-coefficient sufficient condition for higher-order SSP Runge--Kutta methods and explicitly notes that sharpness is not guaranteed. No located source states the exact SSPRK(3,3) L2 CFL threshold for this sparse-grid DG operator or the contraction-to-disk reduction with matching alternating-mode necessity. Originality is asserted only to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The result closes an explicit sharpness gap in a recent sparse-grid DG analysis, raises the certified SSPRK(3,3) time-step ceiling by about 25.64 percent over the SSP-coefficient bound, and gives a reusable two-sided reduction for other Runge--Kutta stability polynomials on the same spatial operator.
